title: Welcome to Grafana Cloud Frontend Observability

blocks.content:
[Grafana Cloud Frontend Observability](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/monitor-applications/frontend-observability/?pg=frontend-observability&plcmt=hero-btn-2&cta=docs) lets you see how real users experience your web app. By collecting telemetry directly from the browser, it helps teams measure performance, detect errors, and monitor interactions across devices, browsers, and network conditions. It's powered by the [Grafana Faro Web SDK](https://github.com/grafana/faro-web-sdk/), a lightweight library that captures real user metrics, errors, logs, and client-side traces.

In this guide, you'll learn how to navigate the Frontend Observability application and send your first metrics from Faro to Frontend Observability Dashboard.

You can follow along with the video below.

### Navigating Frontend Observability



We'll start by learning how to get around the Frontend Observability app.

Open the navigation menu and select **Frontend** under the **Observability** section.

[TODO: HOW CAN I ENSURE THE NAVIGATION NEAR FRONTEND IS OPEN]
The first tab of the app is **Frontend**. Every dashboard you've created lives here (active, stale, and no data), and you can search for a specific one.
The second tab is **Errors**. Here you can see every error across your applications and filter them by dashboard name, error, and version.
The third tab is **Configuration**. Here you can see your alert setup, enable or disable alerts, and view the apps each alert is associated with.
The final tab is **Learn**. Here you'll find essential Frontend Observability resources, from documentation to guides, to help you get more out of Frontend Observability.
Let's head back to the **Frontend** tab and create our first Frontend Observability dashboard.

blocks.content: Select **Create New** to create a new Frontend Observability dashboard.
Give your application a unique name and add the domain you want to monitor, so Frontend Observability knows which frontend to collect and analyze data for.

Let's connect our web application. You have 4 options based on preference we recommend you choose choose manual instrumentation

Once selected you will see instrumentation directions for setting up faro to send metrics to Frontend Observability
